newsitem.title: UK: Natwest European fixed income head quits.
newsitem.headline: Natwest European fixed income head quits.

text.p: NatWest Market's European fixed income head Johan Hattingh has resigned from the firm, banking sources said on Friday, adding his resignation was not linked to the firm's interest rate options losses.

Hattingh was managing director of European fixed income at the investment banking arm of Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc. NatWest Markets on Thursday suspended four senior employees after revealing losses of 90 million pounds ($143.5 million) in interest rate options.
NatWest Markets said Hattingh's departure was due to an internal reorganisation at the firm. This follows its $590 million acquisition of U.S. bond trading house Greenwich Capital in June last year.
"He is leaving as a result of the reorganisation and restructuring of the debt markets division," a NatWest spokeswoman told Reuters.
On Thursday a NatWest internal inquiry into losses in its interest rate options book revealed that the losses had built up over a period of more than two years.

The firm said it had clawed back eight million pounds ($12.8 million) in bonuses from a handful of staff in its global debt derivatives division and NatWest Markets' chief executive had sacrificed 200,000 of his 500,000 pound 1996 bonus. ($ = 0.627 British Pounds)
